To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mothers of the mentally challenged child perceived lower subjective well being, social support, hope, and higher stress and coping than non caregiving mothers of normal children.
the mothers who had normal children (Non caregiving mothers) perceived higher subjective well-being and social support than mothers who had mentally challenged children (Caregiving mothers).
caregiving mothers perceived lower subjective well being, social support and feeling of hope, higher stress and used less effective and more ineffective coping mechanisms than non caregiving mothers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of subjective well being, social support, hope, stress and the coping mechanism among mothers of mentally challenged children and mothers of normal children.
the subjective well being, social support, hope, stress and their coping mechanisms among the mothers of normal children and mentally challenged children.
the relationship among subjective well being, social support, hope, stress and caregiving.
